I've been working this land in Quzhou for 20 years. No one taught me in a classroom — I learned by watching the soil, watching the sky, and watching what my neighbors do. My father farmed before me. That's my education.

My land is 379.9 mu. Cotton is the main business — it's what this county is known for, and it's what I know how to sell. I'll put about 280 mu into cotton. The remaining 100 mu I'll plant summer maize. Maize feeds the family and the animals, and when prices are good I sell some too.

For cotton, I plant in late April after the soil warms. I've been using hybrid Bt cotton seed for years — the bollworm pressure here is serious and I can't afford to lose a crop to pests. I plough before planting, same as always. I fertilize heavier on nitrogen because cotton on this sandy-loam soil needs it. I pump from the well four times across the season — at seedling stage, boll formation, and twice during peak summer heat. I'll spray pesticides about six times — aphids and spider mites are bad most years. I expect around 280 kg per mu of seed cotton if the weather cooperates.

For maize, I plant in mid-June after the spring busy season. Hybrid seed, same as everyone around here. I use rotary tillage since I'm following cotton preparation. Maize doesn't need as many inputs — three irrigations, two pesticide passes for corn borer. Yield should be around 550 kg per mu.

I don't take risks with new methods. I do what has worked for 20 years.
